nodes.label: Inherited Rule Filter Set
nodes.rationale: The adapter owns zero rules and zero rule semantics. Inherited keys stay javascript:S and css:S, and eligibility is expressed as a formula over the owning catalogs precisely to prevent numeric-key duplication or ownership transfer; the adapter only changes eligibility and coordinates.

nodes.label: Strict Non-Ownership of Host Measures
nodes.rationale: Even though the fragment analyzer computes temporary snippet NCLOC internally, host NCLOC, comments, complexity, highlighting, symbols, CPD and coverage stay with the HTML, Infrastructure-as-Code or JavaScript host owner, so two analyzers can never both claim one host file's measures.

nodes.label: ERB Evidence Filter
nodes.rationale: Bare .erb files are admitted only on a recognized preceding extension or HTML evidence inside the first 2,048 characters, precisely to stop generic text, YAML or Dockerfile ERB templates from being treated as HTML solely because of the suffix. A read failure deliberately keeps the file so the normal sensor error path stays visible.

nodes.label: HTML and JSP Language Registration
nodes.rationale: One plugin defines both the web and jsp languages and additionally claims a fixed PHP/Vue suffix set that neither configurable suffix property can remove, so HTML-bearing host formats are structurally inspected without transferring host-language ownership.

nodes.label: HTML Measure Ownership Boundary
nodes.rationale: Measures, line NCLOC, highlighting and CPD are produced only when the input language is absent, web or jsp; a PHP or Vue file selected by fixed suffix may receive HTML issues but never HTML measures, because its owning language analyzer remains authoritative.

nodes.label: Tolerant Page Lexer and Hierarchy Recovery
nodes.norm_label: tolerant page lexer and hierarchy recovery

nodes.label: Azure Resource Manager and Bicep Family
nodes.norm_label: azure resource manager and bicep family

nodes.label: Excluded Enterprise IaC Sensors
nodes.rationale: No Ansible, Azure Pipelines, GitHub Actions or other commercial IaC sensor, rule, profile or file-type claim follows from the shared enum names and predicates that remain visible in the Community artifact.

nodes.label: Helm Native Helper Subprocess
nodes.rationale: Five packaged per-platform helper executables render templates in a fresh subprocess per template with a five-second ceiling, so chart evaluation never runs a Helm command, fetches a remote repository or contacts a cluster, and rendered locations are projected back to the original template.

nodes.label: JVM Framework Configuration Family
nodes.rationale: This sensor deliberately reuses the existing java language and rule repository instead of defining a new one, and it does not advertise independent-file processing because a Spring, Micronaut or Quarkus profile may span several documents or files.

nodes.label: Shared File Type Classifier
nodes.rationale: One cached pre-analysis classifier assigns exactly one type per input in a fixed first-match order, which is what prevents competing IaC families from both claiming the same YAML or JSON file; the GitHub Actions entry exists only to reserve those files against misclassification, not to analyze them.

nodes.label: Excluded Commercial JavaScript Rule Bundles
nodes.rationale: Commercial rule bundles and private analyzers are outside the contract; the packaged ESLint plugin distribution, build/test tooling, telemetry back end and third-party parser implementations are treated as dependencies rather than independently re-specified products.

nodes.label: JavaScript and TypeScript Combined Exclusions
nodes.rationale: JavaScript and TypeScript deliberately share one exclusion surface: if either sonar.javascript.exclusions or sonar.typescript.exclusions is present, both configured arrays are concatenated and replace all defaults, so the two analyzers over one runtime cannot disagree about which files exist.

nodes.label: JavaScript File Recognition and Generated-Source Detection
nodes.norm_label: javascript file recognition and generated-source detection

nodes.label: Node.js Runtime Selection and Provisioning
nodes.rationale: Precedence sonar.nodejs.executable, then provisioned embedded runtime, then host runtime lets operators pin a runtime without losing the zero-configuration embedded path. A failed runtime is not immediately retried: restart becomes eligible only after a prior healthy state has been absent for more than 60 seconds, avoiding restart storms on a broken host.

nodes.label: Shared Bridge and Runtime Contract
nodes.rationale: Declared authoritative for the JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS and embedded Web/YAML specifications so dependent files reference it and never redefine process selection, transport, lease, cache envelope or Node lifecycle. One project sensor collects js, ts, css, web and eligible yaml inputs and sends a single project request over one loopback gRPC channel, so four externally distinct analyzers are one running artifact underneath.

nodes.label: Orphan Program Fallback and Type-Checking Gates
nodes.norm_label: orphan program fallback and type-checking gates
nodes.rationale: Orphan programs exist so accepted files absent from every tsconfig still receive type information, grouped by effective ECMAScript library. When type checking or orphan creation is disabled the file degrades to syntax-only rather than being dropped, and type-dependent rules are sanitized to no-op because missing type information must never be replaced with guessed types.

nodes.label: Clean-Room Source and Pseudocode Prohibition
nodes.rationale: Public compatibility identifiers may be preserved because independent implementations require them, but implementation source, pseudocode, copied comments, decompiled output and source-language examples are prohibited so the corpus stays clean-room.

nodes.label: Per-Part Specification Contract
nodes.rationale: Every specification must carry identity, capabilities, inputs, outputs, processing, state, configuration, failure behavior, limits, security boundaries, acceptance scenarios and traceability so an independent team can derive expected behavior without access to the upstream checkout.

nodes.label: Strong-Copyleft Copy Marker
nodes.rationale: Only GPL and AGPL trees receive a provenance copy marker instead of a behavioral specification; LGPL, MPL, EPL, permissive, source-available, proprietary and unclear terms are treated conservatively and receive full specifications.

nodes.label: Global Constraints
nodes.rationale: Constraints force a pinned release, per-subtree license decisions, cited provenance for every capability, and an explicit separation of observed facts from inference, so missing behavior is reported rather than invented.

nodes.label: License Classification Rule
nodes.rationale: Classification is applied to the smallest practical source subtree rather than inferred from repository ownership, so a differently licensed embedded or generated tree cannot be hidden by a repository-level label.

nodes.label: Subtree and Packaged-Dependency Exceptions
nodes.rationale: Dual-licensed or vendored payloads affect provenance and redistribution but do not convert their containing Sonar-owned trees into GPL or AGPL trees, so no copy-marker shortcut applies to them.

nodes.label: Explicit Exclusions
nodes.rationale: Commercial artifacts, example plugins, build machinery and third-party implementations are excluded as products because they are not bundled by Community Build assembly or are not Sonar-owned behavior; only their Sonar-facing interoperability stays in scope.

nodes.label: Provenance Limitations
nodes.rationale: Some released artifacts publish immutable source archives but no matching public Git tag, so the exact artifacts and hashes are authoritative and release-boundary commits are recorded as corroboration only.

nodes.label: Baseline Rule
nodes.rationale: Later branch or release behavior is out of scope unless it only clarifies an unchanged pinned-release contract, preventing newer upstream behavior from leaking into the specified release.

nodes.label: Common Error Envelope
nodes.rationale: Unhandled failures return a generic client message while the exception detail is logged and never copied into the response, and a failure after a committed stream can only be logged.

nodes.label: Representation and Media-Type Selection
nodes.rationale: A recognized URL suffix outranks the Accept header, which makes protobuf and JSON selection deterministic for release-coupled clients.

nodes.label: Request Validation and Parameter Precedence
nodes.rationale: Required validation checks whether a raw value was supplied rather than whether a default exists, and a supplied deprecated key outranks its replacement key.

nodes.label: Route Spaces and Dispatch
nodes.rationale: Moved legacy component actions are rerouted by execution rather than by HTTP redirect, so existing clients keep their request parameters and response conventions.

nodes.label: Canonical Community Table Inventory
nodes.rationale: Schema names for capabilities unavailable in Community Build are recorded only because the pinned migration registry manipulates them; their presence asserts no feature behavior.

nodes.label: Charset and Collation Invariants
nodes.rationale: Nonconforming PostgreSQL collations fail the check rather than being rewritten and a SQL Server database with an invalid default collation is rejected instead of globally rewritten, because a silent global rewrite would be destructive.

nodes.label: Schema Version States
nodes.rationale: No downgrade steps are provided, so a database recorded above the registry maximum is reported as requiring downgrade rather than being silently accepted.

nodes.label: Release Baseline
nodes.rationale: One reproducible stable release is pinned by tag, commit and distribution checksum, and branch heads are never substituted, so every specification describes the same immutable artifact set.

nodes.label: Writer Coordination
nodes.rationale: Contract ownership is assigned before writers start so cross-cutting parts can be written independently and in parallel without creating competing shared specifications.

nodes.label: Non-Ownership Rules
nodes.rationale: Shared wire formats and state machines are referenced rather than restated so one owner defines each contract: an analyzer owns only language-specific computation, an integration owns only external protocol behavior, and third-party runtimes stay dependencies rather than Sonar parts.

nodes.label: Anticipated Transitions
nodes.rationale: The requesting user's permission is rechecked at consumption time during analysis, so entries belonging to a user whose rights were revoked are ignored.

nodes.label: Code-Quality Issue Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Automatic close records the previous status and resolution, so an issue that becomes live again restores its prior state instead of reappearing as a new finding.

nodes.label: Hotspot-to-Issue Migration
nodes.rationale: Migration rewrites the existing issue row rather than creating a replacement, preserving key, comments and changelog, and keyset-paged batches mean a crash loses only the active batch while a rerun resumes.

nodes.label: Normalized Issue Status Projection
nodes.rationale: Legacy status, resolution, severity and type fields remain present for compatibility while the normalized issue status is the preferred lifecycle projection.

nodes.label: Issue Integration and Tracking
nodes.rationale: Unchanged files may reuse prior issues without tracking unless an involved analyzer plugin changed after that analysis, which keeps issue identity stable while still re-evaluating changed rule behavior.

nodes.label: Ordered Report Processing Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Steps run in a fixed order and stop at the first failure, and post-analysis extensions receive overall success only when every active ordered step completed, so partial results are never published as a successful analysis.

nodes.label: Queue Recovery, Cleanup and Retention
nodes.rationale: A cluster-wide cleanup lock resets orphaned in-progress rows and cancels worn-out pending rows so a lost worker cannot strand a task, while a purge failure leaves data intact for the next daily attempt.

nodes.label: Transaction Boundary Contract
nodes.rationale: Several operations deliberately commit inside the DAO - atomic queue claiming, streamed writes, phased purges - so an implementation must preserve those observed narrower boundaries instead of wrapping every facade call in an assumed all-or-nothing transaction.

nodes.label: L1: File Content, No Semantics
nodes.rationale: Secrets and Unicode-security checks need only decoded file content.

nodes.label: L2: Structural File Analysis
nodes.rationale: IaC misconfiguration needs one parse tree but no dependency or classpath.

nodes.label: L3: Tokens and Parse Tree
nodes.rationale: Style, naming, duplication, and code smells need only file-local syntax.

nodes.label: L4: Lockfile Coordinate
nodes.rationale: Vulnerable-dependency matching needs only the committed coordinate and version.

nodes.label: L6: Import Graph, No Classpath
nodes.rationale: Cross-file taint and first-party call edges need import-scoped binding.

nodes.label: L7: Fetched Declarations
nodes.rationale: External symbol attribution needs public declarations but no build or package manager.

nodes.label: L8: Type Checker + Classpath
nodes.rationale: Exact overloads, generic instantiation, and inheritance-precise dispatch need whole-program type inference.

nodes.label: L9: Statically Undecidable Wiring
nodes.rationale: Runtime wiring cannot be resolved statically; sites are counted instead.

nodes.label: Question Cost: A Ladder, Not a Ladder-Climb
nodes.norm_label: question cost: a ladder, not a ladder-climb

nodes.label: Embedded Relational Store
nodes.rationale: Join-and-reachability queries need relational joins and recursive traversal; flat files or key-value storage would reimplement both.

nodes.label: No Product Goal Requires L8
nodes.rationale: L8 raises precision for a bounded minority of deterministic findings, while codebase understanding and blast radius bottom out at L6–L7.

nodes.label: Rank Features by Their Question’s Required Input
nodes.norm_label: rank features by their question’s required input
nodes.rationale: The correct comparison asks what each output honestly requires, not what inputs a competitor’s sandbox happens to reach.

nodes.norm_label: jacoco report path configuration and fallback precedence

nodes.rationale: Named but not specified; a future user-configured route to option D, and no current capability may depend on it.

nodes.label: CodeQL Java build-mode: none
nodes.rationale: A production parse-and-resolve path that invokes Maven or Gradle only for dependency information, never compilation, accepting documented precision losses.

nodes.norm_label: how coderabbit reviews without touching the build

nodes.norm_label: generated source option d: run the generator
nodes.rationale: Forbidden as an engine decision by the no-build rule; only a future user-directed mechanism may reach it.

nodes.label: No-Build Rule
nodes.rationale: Nothing is compiled or executed because reproducing somebody else’s build cannot be made reliably predictable; the rule also removes build-system support, sandbox, credential, and provenance machinery.

nodes.label: Type Resolution Disabled by Default
nodes.rationale: Type-aware ESLint is disabled and Infer Java is off because compilation cost exceeds flagship review latency.

nodes.label: Zero CI or Build-Plugin Requirement
nodes.rationale: The customer installs a forge app and grants review access; no CI step or customer-produced analysis artifact is required.

nodes.label: Resolve, Don’t Compile
nodes.rationale: Industry default separates dependency discovery from compilation, but the later settled product rule tightens this further to declarations and pinned artifacts without invoking a resolver.

nodes.label: Aikido Security Engine Stack and No-Build Claim
nodes.norm_label: aikido security engine stack and no-build claim

nodes.label: How Shipping Products Get Results Without a Build
nodes.norm_label: how shipping products get results without a build

nodes.norm_label: snyk build requirements by product and language

nodes.label: Adopt JDT Java resolver verdict
nodes.rationale: With a classpath JDT resolves effectively every reference and call at about 20 ms per kLOC with stable overload-specific keys, while the classpath-free floor retains 57.7 percent trustworthy references; recovered bindings are rejected because recovery is non-transitive and often names the wrong symbol.

nodes.label: Rung 2 opportunistic classpath acquisition scope status
nodes.norm_label: rung 2 opportunistic classpath acquisition scope status

nodes.label: Excluded Commercial Python Enterprise Plugin
nodes.rationale: The separate enterprise artifact is declared by the product build for other editions, so its behavior is excluded here rather than inferred from the Community artifact.

nodes.label: Notebook Analysis Exclusions
nodes.rationale: Server-side notebook caching is disabled, notebooks stay out of the project-level global symbol table, no notebook CPD tokens or per-line ncloc_data are emitted and notebook executable-line data is empty, because the generated Python view is a projection rather than a real indexed source file.

nodes.label: Notebook Location Mapping
nodes.rationale: Notebook JSON is transformed into one in-memory Python stream that is never written as a user-visible source file; every syntax node, issue, secondary location, highlight, symbol, measure and analysis error is projected back to the original notebook coordinates, including the escape and compressed-single-line offsets recorded per generated line.

nodes.label: Project-Level Symbol Table and Package Indexing
nodes.norm_label: project-level symbol table and package indexing

nodes.label: Public-Artifact Facts Index
nodes.rationale: Ships declarations and safe interface facts keyed by coordinate and hash as local data, excluding comments, bodies, source, and bytecode fragments by schema.

nodes.label: Reachability Into Dependency Code Without Compiling the Target
nodes.norm_label: reachability into dependency code without compiling the target

nodes.label: Facts-Only Index Licence Decision
nodes.rationale: Published interface declarations and edges are functional facts; the shared schema must structurally forbid expressive comments, bodies, source, and bytecode fragments.

nodes.label: Public Dependency-Side Precomputation
nodes.rationale: Only public version-pinned artifacts are identical and safely reusable across customers; first-party roots remain customer-local.

nodes.label: Adopt opportunistic bytecode tier verdict
nodes.rationale: The tier yields 961 dependency and platform call edges plus exact annotation references that source-only analysis misses, but it depends on compilable classes; rapid-type analysis is required and the JDK image is excluded because class-hierarchy analysis explodes to millions of noisy edges.

nodes.label: Embedded Native Go Parser Executables
nodes.rationale: Five packaged per-platform executables are extracted to a temporary directory and a fresh subprocess handles each directory-sized batch, so same-package files are parsed and type-checked together while a syntax error in one file still leaves valid siblings usable in the same process result.

nodes.label: Go Measures Symbols Highlighting and CPD
nodes.norm_label: go measures symbols highlighting and cpd

nodes.label: Excluded Commercial Text Plugins
nodes.rationale: The developer and enterprise artifacts are not bundled and their source archives and pattern inventories are absent from the authoritative public archive, so their rule keys, pattern IDs, formats and filters are unavailable; this is an explicit scope boundary, not an incomplete Community catalog.

nodes.label: File Eligibility and Git Status Gating
nodes.norm_label: file eligibility and git status gating

nodes.label: Secret Candidate Filters and Confidence
nodes.rationale: Disabling the entropy or known-fake filter does not remove the constraint from the catalog; a candidate that fails only a skippable filter is emitted with a low-confidence annotation naming the disabled filters, while hard format constraints, path exclusions, auxiliary context and MAIN-file scope remain active.

nodes.label: Suffixless Language Registration
nodes.rationale: The text and secrets languages register zero file suffixes on purpose: they exist to own rules and quality profiles, not to claim files, so files keep the language assignment made by other analyzers and this artifact owns content selection and issue production instead of language recognition.

nodes.label: Project, Rule, Profile, Gate and Metric Identifiers
nodes.norm_label: project, rule, profile, gate and metric identifiers

nodes.label: Durable Compute Task Queue
nodes.rationale: Claiming uses a conditional PENDING-to-IN_PROGRESS update so only one worker wins, and workers alternate their first-choice poll between report work and issue-index synchronization so neither class starves.

nodes.label: Report Part Splitting
nodes.rationale: The configured part threshold is multiplied using signed 32-bit arithmetic and is not range-checked, so only 1 through 2047 MiB are usable and boundary values fail or overflow instead of being corrected.

nodes.label: Report Submission and Acknowledgement
nodes.rationale: Acknowledgement means only that report parts are stored and a compute task is durably queued; the gateway never parses or validates protobuf content during upload, so payload errors surface later as task failures.

nodes.label: Measure Computation Families
nodes.rationale: A CE-computed value takes precedence over a later scanner value, unregistered metric keys are ignored, and empty or best-value-optimized measures are not persisted, which keeps stored measures canonical and compact.

nodes.label: Metric Registration Contract
nodes.rationale: Duplicate metric keys are fatal registration errors and quality-gate conditions referring to invalid metrics are deleted during registration, so the metric vocabulary cannot become ambiguous.

nodes.label: Quality Gate Selection and Evaluation
nodes.rationale: An explicit project association wins over the installation default, and the absence of a default gate is an invalid server state that fails resolution rather than choosing an arbitrary gate.

nodes.label: Quality Profile and Active-Rule Resolution
nodes.rationale: A project association replaces only its own language's default profile and an active-rule parameter override wins over the rule default, so the effective configuration is deterministic per language.

nodes.label: Rule Registration and Rule State
nodes.rationale: A rule whose whole repository disappeared keeps its active rules for compatibility, while a rule dropped from a still-present repository is marked removed and unbound, so profile change history stays meaningful.

nodes.label: Stable Identifier and Component Model
nodes.rationale: A public project key is mutable while the internal UUID is immutable, so renaming updates descendant component keys without breaking UUID-based associations.

nodes.label: Scanner Referential Views
nodes.rationale: When a project key does not resolve, default active rules are returned rather than a not-found error, so a first analysis of an unknown project can still bootstrap.

nodes.label: Cross-Repository Resolution
nodes.rationale: Matches lockfile coordinates to reviewed repositories and resolves against the pinned tag or commit, recording the answering ref.

nodes.label: Private Readable-Source Repository Route
nodes.rationale: Resolve private dependencies from a repository the reviewer can read at the ref the target pins.

nodes.label: Code Graph Sourcing: Build, Improve, or Consume
nodes.norm_label: code graph sourcing: build, improve, or consume

nodes.label: No Private Registry Rule
nodes.rationale: Avoid making the engine credential-bearing in the customer supply chain when reviewed sibling sources provide the expected route.

nodes.label: Runner Persistence and Warm-Up
nodes.rationale: Caches, base-ref facts, sibling indexes, toolchains, and resident processes are components to provision, not fidelity constraints.

nodes.label: Exactly Two Dependency-Resolution Routes
nodes.rationale: Resolution is limited to reproducible authority: public pinned artifacts or readable source repositories for private dependencies.

nodes.label: Coordinate-Based Cross-Repository Link
nodes.rationale: A lockfile coordinate matching a repository’s published coordinate is a deterministic first-review link, unlike gradually inferred agent research.

nodes.label: Customer-Operated Runner
nodes.rationale: Caches, credentials, toolchains, and persistent state already sit inside the customer perimeter, so many vendor-hosted workarounds become provisioning concerns.

nodes.label: Curated Library API Model
nodes.rationale: Models sources, sinks, sanitizers, and dangerous signatures by name and shape so flaw finding does not require resolving dependency internals.

nodes.label: L5: File + Curated API Model
nodes.rationale: Single-file taint needs local scope plus modelled source and sink signatures.

nodes.label: Snyk Reachability Under-Approximation
nodes.rationale: No path found is not proof of unreachability; reflection and the accuracy/recall trade-off keep negative answers explicitly qualified.

nodes.label: Sole Storage Contract Owner
nodes.rationale: Every stateful part reuses one connection, transaction, schema, migration, and observability contract instead of defining another.

nodes.label: Thin JDBC Sessions
nodes.rationale: An ORM would add a second configuration lifecycle and statement dialect without product value.

nodes.label: Migration First-Failure Stop
nodes.rationale: Successful prior steps remain durable; the failed step is absent from history and retry resumes after the last recorded success.

nodes.label: No Reverse Migrations
nodes.rationale: With no legacy installed base, a newer schema is recovered by operator restore rather than reverse migration machinery.

nodes.label: Persistence Dialect and Migration Trim
nodes.rationale: A single-operator local engine owns one embedded file, so the external PostgreSQL dialect, DDL abstraction, embedded TCP server, and durable migration history are unnecessary; schema mismatch can wipe and rebuild until user-authored state exists.

nodes.label: cls-meta.xml Mandatory Exclusion
nodes.rationale: Every path matching the cls-meta.xml pattern is excluded after language classification, and the exclusion is mandatory even when a suffix override explicitly classifies the file as XML, so a configuration change cannot reintroduce those metadata files.

nodes.label: Config Parse-Failure Tolerance
nodes.rationale: A parse failure on a lowercase .config filename is silently skipped with no analysis error, issue, measure or highlighting, accommodating the convention of naming non-XML files .config; the exemption deliberately does not extend to .xml, .xsd, .xsl or uppercase .CONFIG.

nodes.label: XML DOM and Source Location Model
nodes.norm_label: xml dom and source location model

nodes.label: XML Rule Catalog and Legacy Mappings
nodes.norm_label: xml rule catalog and legacy mappings

nodes.label: Configuration Precedence
nodes.rationale: Configuration file, environment, -D application arguments, and JVM properties override in order; defaults apply only when unset, and invalid explicit values fail loudly.

nodes.label: Trusted Local Resources
nodes.rationale: Write access to home, config, data, or logs controls what the engine reads or reports, so ownership must be restricted to the engine account.

nodes.label: Eclipse JDT Core
nodes.rationale: Adopted for Java because it provides real ECJ bindings from a classpath without building the target and is embeddable on the JVM.

nodes.label: Kotlin Analysis API Standalone
nodes.rationale: Adopted through per-language-version workers because compiler versions are target-specific and must not share a service classloader.

nodes.label: Public-and-Pinned Artifact Route
nodes.rationale: Fetch a public artifact by target-declared coordinate and lockfile hash; never invoke a package manager.

nodes.label: Two-Phase Fetch and Analyse Split
nodes.rationale: Coordinates may come from a contribution but hosts may not; fetching chooses bytes under a base-ref allowlist, then analysis reads them offline as hostile data.

nodes.label: Worker Process Isolation
nodes.rationale: Compiler and archive processing over hostile data needs heap caps, deadlines, crash containment, and version isolation even though target code never executes.

nodes.label: Generated Source Option C: Read Committed Output
nodes.norm_label: generated source option c: read committed output
nodes.rationale: Free coverage because committed generated code is ordinary source.

nodes.label: Semgrep Syntactic Interfile Analysis
nodes.rationale: Whole-project name resolution populates identifier information and feeds heuristic type inference, constant propagation, and taint without compiled code.

nodes.label: Conservative Under-Approximation
nodes.rationale: Only marks code unreachable with high confidence; ambiguous graph cases remain visible at higher severity.

nodes.label: Leveret Inspect
nodes.rationale: A single-operator code-intelligence and code-review engine for developers and coding agents, not an enterprise governance platform.

nodes.label: One-Process Synchronous Analysis
nodes.rationale: Removes web/worker fleet topology while still allowing compiler frontends to be isolated in workers for hostile input.

nodes.label: Scanner/Server Split Removal
nodes.rationale: Goals 4 and 5 need the graph itself; serializing findings through a producer/server queue is lossy and adds five dependent transport capabilities.

nodes.label: Single-Operator Deployment
nodes.rationale: The engine runs for one operator and their agents on one machine and grants no access beyond the filesystem account.

nodes.label: Sunk Cost Is Not an Argument
nodes.norm_label: sunk cost is not an argument
nodes.rationale: Already-written runtime and persistence machinery is removed when the product shape no longer needs it.

nodes.label: Deferred Mechanism G: Source-Unavailable Private Dependency
nodes.norm_label: deferred mechanism g: source-unavailable private dependency
nodes.rationale: Named but not specified; covers vendor-supplied, binary-only, or archived private dependencies whose source cannot be granted.

nodes.label: Missing Authority Report
nodes.rationale: Unavailable authority is detected and rendered with coordinates, affected references, and the exact grant that would close the gap rather than treated as a design constraint.

nodes.label: Dropped Alias Property Prefix
nodes.rationale: The upstream release marks the alias property prefix and a second configuration file name as release-coupled for interoperability with its own scanners and operator tooling. Leveret Inspect is the only consumer of this node, so those identifiers carry no compatibility value here and are not reproduced: the property prefix is leveret. only, accepted in no other spelling in the configuration file, environment names, application arguments, or system properties, and conf/leveret.properties is the sole base configuration file. The specification's behavior is implemented; its vendor-specific spellings are not.

nodes.label: Dropped Cluster Mode
nodes.rationale: Multi-node clustering is not implemented in any form, because Leveret Inspect will not use it: no cluster-activation setting is recognized, the restart-rejection branch that setting would guard does not exist, and no cluster node name labels log records. This is out of scope by decision rather than deferral, so no partial multi-node coordination exists to mislead a later reader.

nodes.label: Dropped Search Engine External-Options Suppression
nodes.rationale: Suppression of the upstream search engine's external-options environment variable exists to protect that vendor's search engine, which Leveret Inspect will not run, so the suppression carries no value here. Suppression of generic JVM tool options is deliberately kept, because it prevents an inherited agent configuration from silently attaching to child processes.

nodes.label: Fixed Hard-Stop Helper Working-Directory Behavior
nodes.rationale: The upstream hard-stop helper resolves a relative temporary path against the caller's working directory and can therefore report success without stopping the node. That quirk is a defect with no compatibility value for the only consumer of this node, so it is fixed rather than reproduced: the standalone requester derives installation home, reads the configuration file from it, and resolves a relative temporary path against that home, so it targets the running node from any working directory.

nodes.label: JDK 25 Bytecode Floor
nodes.rationale: Kotlin on the JVM with bytecode target JDK 25, the current long-term-support release. Kotlin 2.4.0 targets 1.8 and 9 through 26, so the floor is a support decision, not a toolchain limit; local builds compile on the installed JDK 26 with release 25.

nodes.label: JVM Options and Command Construction Unit
nodes.norm_label: jvm options and command construction unit

nodes.label: Provisional Search Readiness Address Keys
nodes.rationale: The search health probe is expressed as an interface with a loopback HTTP implementation addressed by leveret.search.host, defaulting to 127.0.0.1, and leveret.search.port, defaulting to 9001. These two keys are a provisional handoff: platform/search-indexing becomes their owner when implemented, so the readiness contract stays behind an interface instead of hard-coding an address.

nodes.label: Renamed Search Process Identity
nodes.rationale: All naming is Leveret Inspect's own. The upstream search process key and log prefix are release-coupled only for the vendor's own scanners and operator tooling, and Leveret Inspect is the only consumer of this node, so that spelling carries no compatibility value: the identity is the process key search at index 1 with log prefix search, log file search.log, and display name Search.

nodes.label: Single Runtime Module with Three Entry Points
nodes.norm_label: single runtime module with three entry points
nodes.rationale: One module rather than four mirrors behavior instead of incidental build structure. The monitor, the standalone hard-stop requester, and the reusable child entry point are separate entry points inside one artifact because children are separate operating-system processes, not separate distributions.

nodes.label: HTTP Startup-Mode State Machine
nodes.rationale: The safe-mode dispatcher stays authoritative until the full container has completed initialization, which prevents requests from observing a partially initialized platform.

nodes.label: Migration History
nodes.rationale: A migration number is written only after its step returns successfully, the history component runs only in the startup-leading web process, and the progress object is not thread-safe, so migration execution must be serialized by startup leadership.

nodes.label: Dependency-Ordered Startup and Readiness
nodes.rationale: Readiness is only the common process-runtime operational signal; it is not a promise that every HTTP feature, background task or index is healthy, because those parts publish their own health within it.

nodes.label: Failure and Recovery Behavior
nodes.rationale: Only failures inside the guarded startup phase are caught and followed by monitor status 0, so operators must use readiness and logs rather than exit status alone to distinguish successful startup from failure.

nodes.label: JVM Option Contract
nodes.rationale: Process-mandatory options such as UTF-8 encoding, headless mode and the runtime temporary directory cannot be replaced, so an attempted mandatory-option override fails command construction instead of silently producing an unsupported child.

nodes.label: Node Lifecycle State Machine
nodes.rationale: Invalid or duplicate transition requests are ignored rather than creating a second transition, and an unexpected child exit hard-stops the whole node instead of restarting one child, which prevents a partially operational node.

nodes.label: Process Identity and Launch Topology
nodes.rationale: Process keys, IPC indexes and log prefixes are release-coupled compatibility identifiers, and later processes are gated on prerequisite readiness rather than launched concurrently.

nodes.label: Restart and Shutdown Escalation
nodes.rationale: Graceful stop follows reverse dependency order and escalates to hard stop and forced destruction on timeout, and immutable path or cluster properties cannot change across an internal restart because continuing with mixed paths would corrupt node state.

nodes.label: Shared-Memory IPC Contract
nodes.rationale: IPC is local memory-mapped file coordination with no authentication or encryption, so filesystem ownership of the temporary directory is part of the trust boundary and hard-stop access is equivalent to local administrative control.

nodes.label: SCIP Optional Import Format
nodes.rationale: Provides stable producer symbols and easy JVM decoding, but lacks confidence, unresolved-reference records, a reliable call role, and delta semantics.

nodes.label: Per-File Failure Isolation and Partial Results
nodes.norm_label: per-file failure isolation and partial results

nodes.label: Standard-Format Finding Interchange
nodes.rationale: One codec pays for delegation to native tools and lets findings reach editors, CI, and agents.

nodes.label: Curated Generator Contract Model
nodes.rationale: Models stable declared output contracts with openly graded generator/version coverage; cheaper and reproducible compared with running or scavenging generators.

nodes.label: Deterministic Findings Consumer
nodes.rationale: Precision dominates; rules remain silent when available basis is weaker than they require.

nodes.label: Import-Scoped Candidate Sets
nodes.rationale: One reachable candidate is a fact; several are labelled ambiguity useful for orientation rather than discarded as failure.

nodes.label: Reviewing-Model Orientation Consumer
nodes.rationale: Recall with labelled uncertainty points the reviewer to relevant code and blind spots, and must always work from files at rest.

nodes.label: Unit-and-Ownership Delta Application
nodes.rationale: Mines Glean’s unit stacking and ownership propagation while keeping the product store and runtime local.

nodes.label: Evidence/Confidence-Labeled Relationship Graph
nodes.rationale: Useful transferable technique: every inferred relationship cites evidence and labels confidence while explicitly admitting incompleteness.

nodes.label: Per-Edge Basis Field
nodes.rationale: Allows checked, declared, documented, import-scoped, scope-local, name-matched, and synthesized facts to coexist without weak facts contaminating impact answers.

nodes.label: platform/code-graph
nodes.rationale: Owns resolved facts agents cannot cheaply recompute: symbols, typed edges, per-edge basis, unresolved references, and delta application.

nodes.label: Discardable Contribution Overlay
nodes.rationale: Facts from unaccepted code must not pollute the accepted graph; promote the overlay only after merge.

nodes.label: Fact Basis Model
nodes.rationale: Per-fact provenance prevents weaker evidence from silently masquerading as checked resolution and supports honest degradation.

nodes.label: Generated Source Option A: Detect and Disclose
nodes.norm_label: generated source option a: detect and disclose
nodes.rationale: Mandatory floor: only an actually failed binding triggers expected-missing, with a declared generator explaining the gap.

nodes.label: Generated Source Option B: Scavenge Disk Output
nodes.norm_label: generated source option b: scavenge disk output
nodes.rationale: Struck because incidental and stale generated output makes analyses non-reproducible and can yield a wrong binding, which is worse than an honest gap.

nodes.label: Generated Source Option E: Model Generator Contracts
nodes.norm_label: generated source option e: model generator contracts
nodes.rationale: Adopted because declared output contracts are reproducible, execution-free, and independent of stale machine state.

nodes.label: Review Is the Only Product
nodes.rationale: Facts, findings, and orientation are evidence entering a review; dashboards, gates, debt ratings, and portfolio reporting are not separate products.

nodes.label: Runtime-Wiring Sites
nodes.rationale: Static analysis cannot resolve runtime wiring, so impact answers count detectable sites and keep guesses separate from counts.

nodes.label: Graphify as Development Tool Only
nodes.rationale: Its inferred narrative graph is useful for comprehension but is outside the product-owned resolved-facts boundary.

nodes.label: Local Grammar Indexer as Development Tool Only
nodes.norm_label: local grammar indexer as development tool only
nodes.rationale: Useful for repository development, but name-matched resolution is insufficient for a sound product graph.

nodes.label: Resolved-Facts Identity Boundary
nodes.rationale: The engine owns facts, impact closures, mechanical edits, and verification scopes; agents own narrative explanation and judgment.

nodes.label: Shared Static-Reachability Blind Spots
nodes.rationale: Reflection, dynamic loading and dispatch, generated code, and dependency-injection wiring remain incomplete even for build-based vendors; builds mainly improve type resolution.

nodes.label: Excluded Commercial Java Repositories
nodes.rationale: Repositories such as javasecurity and javabugs are not bundled Community capabilities and must not be inferred from the optional reflective integration points left in the built-in profile code.

nodes.label: JaCoCo Coverage Ownership Boundary
nodes.rationale: JaCoCo XML import is owned solely by the separate JaCoCo integration; the Java plugin imports no coverage at all and only warns about the removed sonar.jacoco.* properties.

nodes.label: Java Frontend Syntax and Semantic Model
nodes.norm_label: java frontend syntax and semantic model
nodes.rationale: Eclipse JDT/ECJ parsing plus binding resolution is the one owned semantic artifact that every check and the separate symbolic-execution plugin consume. Binding recovery permits partial semantic analysis on incomplete bytecode but never fabricates resolved symbols, so the safe degradation is fewer findings rather than guessed ones.

nodes.label: Exploded Graph Walker and Program State
nodes.norm_label: exploded graph walker and program state

nodes.label: Main-Source-Only Registration Boundary
nodes.rationale: The registrar calls only registerMainSharedCheck and registerMainChecks, never the test equivalents, so the pinned engine never symbolically executes test-classified files even when a rule's legacy metadata scope says All. Runtime registration is authoritative over metadata scope.

nodes.label: Method Behavior Cache and Bundled Models
nodes.norm_label: method behavior cache and bundled models
nodes.rationale: Source-derived summaries are restricted to methods that cannot be overridden so the engine never assumes a dynamically dispatched implementation. Bundled hardcoded JSON behaviors are trusted plugin data that project inputs cannot replace, and a missing model reduces precision instead of fabricating yields.

nodes.label: Symbolic Execution Rule Catalog
nodes.rationale: The 23 keys extend the existing java repository rather than creating a second repository, so profiles stay unified; they are nonetheless excluded from the Java analyzer's own 714-rule catalog because a different artifact implements them.

nodes.label: Symbolic Exploration Hard Limits
nodes.rationale: Exploration is intentionally bounded and a limit exception is caught at method scope, so one oversized method is abandoned with a debug log while the rest of the file still analyzes. Checks that require complete exploration receive an interrupted-execution callback and discard partial conclusions rather than reporting from a truncated graph.

nodes.label: Embedded Kotlin Compiler and K2 Session
nodes.norm_label: embedded kotlin compiler and k2 session
nodes.rationale: All selected files are presented to one JVM-only K2 session as a single source module so cross-file semantic resolution is available before any file visitor runs. The compiler environment is disposed and the global ZIP handle cache cleared afterwards specifically so a later Windows build can replace dependency archives.

nodes.label: Kotlin Coverage Ownership Boundary
nodes.rationale: The artifact contains no coverage parser at all: Kotlin/JVM coverage is supplied by the bundled JaCoCo integration, and this analyzer contributes only source identity and executable-line data.

nodes.label: Kotlin Gradle DSL Recognition
nodes.rationale: Selection is by exact filename build.gradle.kts or settings.gradle.kts rather than by suffix, so arbitrary Kotlin scripts are excluded and the Gradle rule set never runs on ordinary .kts files.

nodes.label: Adopt Kotlin Analysis API K2 verdict
nodes.norm_label: adopt kotlin analysis api k2 verdict
nodes.rationale: The standalone K2 route resolves all 2,839 references, including 1,119 library and platform symbols, matches the pinned Kotlin 2.4.0 toolchain, and avoids a second language runtime; kotlin2cpg remains an out-of-process fallback, while the scip-java plugin cannot load on Kotlin 2.4.0.
